title: “One-Size-Fits-All”? Examining Expectations around What Constitute “Fair” or “Good” NLG System Behaviors

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of first names and parental roles (e.g., Mom vs. Dad) in input messages to evaluate whether NLG systems make inappropriate gender assumptions (such as pronouns) in their reply suggestions, and analyzing human expectations of these behaviors.

Perturbing input messages with names strongly associated with different racial and ethnic groups to observe differences in system-generated replies and identify unwarranted identity-related assumptions.

Substituting country names from different world regions with varying GDPs in message prompts to evaluate whether NLG systems generate culturally stereotyped, insensitive, or disparate reply suggestions regarding activities and travel.

Comparing NLG system reply behaviors and human usability ratings when input messages contain African American English (AAE) syntactic features (e.g., habitual be, multiple negation) versus General American English (GAE), as well as informal web text versus formal styles.
